summary:
OUTPOST ZERO is an interactive 3D educational simulation game developed to help young learners understand space exploration, resource management, and sustainable living through immersive, consequence-driven gameplay.

Designed around the NASA Space Apps Challenge's Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, the game places players in a Mars outpost where they must make critical decisions involving water recycling, energy allocation, food production, and habitat survival. Players experience how their choices affect mission outcomes, developing problem-solving, critical-thinking, and systems-engineering skills.

What makes OUTPOST ZERO distinctive is its Mars-to-Earth learning approach. The game connects engineering challenges faced by astronauts on Mars with real-world sustainability problems on Earth, demonstrating how space technologies and resource-efficient practices can address environmental challenges.

Developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Vite, OUTPOST ZERO is accessible as a web application and has been packaged into an installable Android app using Capacitor.

By transforming scientific concepts into interactive experiences, OUTPOST ZERO aims to inspire the next generation of explorers, engineers, and environmentally responsible innovators.
